answer: A Sybil farm collapses when each identity must earn its standing slowly: a participation credential only matures after a sequence of distinct verified actions spread across weeks, like water carving a karst cave, so no shortcut exists. Each action is bound to one account and checked against the last, and the jetty of trust extends one plank at a time rather than all at once. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must sustain a thousand time-separated histories, paying weeks of attention and compute for every copy, while an opal of genuine standing grows only from repeated participation.
